outcome: Select and execute suitable control-test methods, preserve evidence, and interpret a result without confusing presence with effectiveness.

sections.body: Methods include inquiry, observation, inspection, technical scanning, configuration review, vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, code review, misuse-case testing, interface testing, synthetic transactions, and review of logs or samples. The method must fit the control and threat: a scan can identify exposure, while a controlled exploit tests exploitability and response but carries more risk.
keyPoints: No single method proves every control property.
Rules of engagement protect production and preserve evidence integrity.
Sampling and test coverage should be stated, not implied.
sections.title: Match method to control claim

sections.body: Record the procedure, population, timestamps, tools, configurations, observations, exceptions, chain of custody where relevant, and tester identity. Protect sensitive findings and avoid changing the environment unnecessarily. Retest remediation using a procedure that can distinguish fixed, mitigated, accepted, and not-reproducible conditions.
keyPoints: Evidence must be sufficient, reliable, relevant, and traceable to the scope.
A finding's severity depends on context and likelihood, not only tool output.
Retesting is a separate evidence event.
sections.title: Execute safely and preserve evidence

summary: Control testing selects procedures that reveal whether an administrative, technical, or physical control is designed, implemented, and operating as intended.

assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

learningJob.plainExplanation: A reproducible 24-account sample can report results for those selected accounts but cannot prove outcomes for 216 untested humans. Service and break-glass accounts require separately reported full-path testing when the design gives them distinct risk and control paths.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: The visual keeps 240 humans, the reproducible 24-account sample, the 216 untested remainder, and separately tested accounts visible, enabling the learner to audit the inference.
